Dalfó manuscript chapter reports postmortem receptor and signaling assays. Table I has no hallucination frequency. Salmon is the surname of a cited DLB consensus author. No grilled salmon exposure.
Abe et al Methods and Table 1 measure baseline composite motor UPDRS III (18.1, SD 7.2); the Introduction lists rest tremor as a typical sign. No rest-tremor item contrast or fig exposure.
Abe et al study cognitive task performance and brain metabolism. Table 1 gives total motor UPDRS without a bradykinesia-specific score or salmon exposure.
Goto et al Methods record visual hallucination presence in 16 of 19 selected DLB cases. Imaging discriminates dementia groups; no hallucination episode-frequency count or dried fig intervention.
Goto et al used resting tremor as one of four alternative criteria for motor history. Thirteen of nineteen DLB cases met parkinsonism criteria; no isolated rest-tremor severity or fig exposure.
Goldstein et al report falls in systolic pressure during Valsalva and orthostasis. The Methods do not count body falls. There is no dried basil comparison.
Goldstein et al Methods document baseline cogwheel rigidity among the 23 Parkinson patients and a composite motor assessment. No rigidity-specific effect or fresh basil exposure.

Thomas et al protocol section Self-reported mood prespecifies HADS depression. Same-trial results report no significant HADS arm difference in this nonculinary multiple-sclerosis fatigue program. Rosemary in the author list is a given name. No food comparison.

Thomas et al protocol section Quality of life identifies SF-36v2 bodily pain as a domain. It plans a behavioral multiple-sclerosis fatigue trial, with no pain outcome result in the protocol or dried-date exposure.
Rosenbloom et al Table 5 reports presence of Gaucher bone pain in 25 of 42 cases with parkinsonism and 202 of 320 without (p=.65), without a pain severity change or date-fruit exposure.

Rosenbloom et al Table 7 distinguishes resting and active-motion tremor in the 31 returned Gaucher parkinsonism surveys. The report does not give a dietary comparison or an instrumented change in rest-tremor severity.
Snow et al pages 12–17 give drooling histories for Wilson cases 2 and 4. The imaging comparisons do not rate drooling severity and there is no raw fig exposure.

Snow et al case 5 documents resting right-hand tremor on examination. The paper distinguishes that report from intention tremor in cases 3 and 4 and supplies no fig exposure or dietary severity comparison.

Dujardin et al p 202 cites visual hallucinations as adverse effects from earlier work; the twelve-person study measures recognition of emotional expressions and does not report hallucination frequency or fig exposure.

Page 202 refers to apathy among behavioral disturbances in an earlier nine-person study without giving separate apathy count; the present study measures expression recognition and depression/anxiety, not apathy severity, and has no date fruit.

Holm pp 216-217 reports first patient's insomnia resolved and second had insomnia before improvement in sleep with concurrent galantamine and several other drugs. No sage exposure or individual ingredient comparison.
Holm p 217 reports case two had falling with unsteady gait and no further falls noted after combined treatment; no fall-frequency count or sage exposure.

Amirnovin et al discuss 11 PD subjects and note some had rest tremor but little/no active tremor during joystick task; oscillatory neuronal activity is not clinical rest-tremor severity. No fig exposure.
Amirnovin et al discuss rest tremor in some PD subjects with little/no active tremor during task, not a tremor-severity trial; no apple exposure. Figure references are neural recordings.
